title: The photos contradict the listing data
when: The listing data names a feature that the photos do not show (for example a pool listed but not in any photo).
steps: Agent 04 (Listing Description) stops: no description is drafted for this listing.
It asks you, naming the conflict ("photos contradict data sheet") and the feature.
never: Describe a feature the photos do not support, or quietly drop it.
why: Advertising a pool that is not there is a misrepresentation claim waiting to happen. You decide which source is right.
you_see: A question naming the feature the photos do not show.
test: A new listing says garage and pool; the photo check finds only a garage. The photographer is booked (you release the booking) and the photos arrive. Nothing goes to Compliance for review.

title: A feature cannot be verified
when: The listing data includes a fact with no source (for example an HVAC year nobody can back up).
steps: Agent 04 leaves the fact out of the description.
It records that it left it out and why, in the client's history.
never: Hedge with "may include" or similar wording.
why: A hedged claim is still a claim. Leaving it out keeps the description to facts you can stand behind.
you_see: The description without the fact; the history notes it was omitted.
test: A new listing includes "HVAC 2015" with no source. The description sent for review does not mention it.

title: Copy you supplied may break fair housing rules
when: Description wording supplied by you or the seller looks like a fair housing problem (for example it rates the schools).
steps: Agent 04 alerts you that the supplied copy is flagged.
It sends the supplied copy to Compliance (Agent 17) for a verdict.
It never rewrites the copy on its own.
never: Rewrite your copy silently, or use it without a compliance verdict.
why: Language about schools or neighborhoods can steer buyers by protected class. Compliance must see the exact words, and you decide the fix.
you_see: A legal-line alert saying the supplied copy was flagged.
test: A new listing comes with the copy "Close to great schools with a high school rating". Today you are alerted, but the copy never goes to Compliance: Agent 04 drafts from the data fields only, so the copy is neither reviewed nor used. How supplied copy is used and reviewed is waiting on your decision.

title: The description is too long: cut adjectives before facts
when: The description does not fit the space available.
steps: Agent 04 cuts descriptive words first.
Facts (bedrooms, bathrooms, square footage) stay.
Source notes ("per county tax records") are never cut.
The draft is marked as cut for length.
never: Cut a fact or a source note to make room for description.
why: Buyers rely on the facts and their sources; adjectives are optional.
you_see: A shorter description that still has every fact and its source.
test: A new listing with twenty long feature phrases. The draft is marked cut for length and still says 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and "per county tax records".

title: A superlative is requested in the description
when: Someone asks for wording like "the best block in town".
steps: Agent 04 declines the superlative and records that it did.
The description is drafted without it.
never: Characterize a neighborhood or block as best, safest or similar.
why: Rating a neighborhood can steer buyers by who lives there, which fair housing law forbids.
you_see: The description without the superlative; the record shows it was declined.
test: A new listing asks: "Call it the best block in town".

title: Square footage differs between the tax record and the seller
when: The tax record and the seller give different square footage.
steps: Agent 04 uses the figure that can be verified (the tax record) and says where it came from.
It tells you about the discrepancy.
It never averages the two.
never: Average the figures or publish the unverified one.
why: A made-up middle number is wrong for certain. The verifiable figure with its source is defensible.
you_see: A question about the discrepancy; the description says "1800 sq ft per county tax records".
test: Tax record 1,800 sq ft; the seller says 2,400. The description says 1,800 per county tax records and never 2,100 (the average).

title: The seller asks to mention schools or neighborhood make-up
when: The seller asks for wording about school quality or who lives in the neighborhood.
steps: Agent 04 refuses that wording and records the refusal.
The draft still goes to Compliance (Agent 17) for its verdict, as every draft does.
never: Put school-quality or demographic wording into a description.
why: These phrases are classic fair housing steering. Compliance reviews every draft regardless.
you_see: The description without the requested wording; Compliance's verdict on the record.
test: A new listing asks: "Please mention the great schools nearby".

title: A photo reveals something about who lives there
when: A listing photo shows an item that reveals protected-class information (for example religious items or family photos).
steps: Agent 04 alerts you before the photos are used anywhere.
No description is sent for review.
never: Use a photo that reveals protected-class information without your review.
why: Such photos can invite discrimination by buyers and expose the seller's privacy.
you_see: A legal-line alert naming the protected-class concern.
test: A new listing whose photo check flags protected-class information. Nothing goes to Compliance for review.

title: A feature comes only from the seller
when: A fact such as roof age comes only from the seller, with no document.
steps: Agent 04 includes it only with its source: "per seller (unverified)".
Without even a stated source, it leaves the fact out.
never: Print a seller's claim as a bare fact.
why: Buyers must be able to tell verified facts from what the seller said.
you_see: The fact in the description with "per seller (unverified)".
test: A new listing with roof age 5, source "per seller". The draft says roof 5, per seller (unverified).

title: Compliance requires changes to a description
when: Compliance (Agent 17) returns its verdict asking for changes.
steps: Agent 04 makes exactly the changes required, no more and no fewer.
It sends the corrected draft back for review.
Only an approved draft is released.
never: Argue with, work around or partly apply a compliance verdict.
why: Compliance is the gate for fair housing. Its verdict is applied as written.
you_see: The released description without the flagged wording.
test: A new listing whose features include "perfect for young families". Compliance flags it, Agent 04 removes it and resubmits, and the released copy does not contain the phrase.

title: The remarks are over the MLS length limit
when: The remarks exceed the MLS field limit.
steps: Agent 04 cuts by the priority list in your settings, whole entries at a time, starting from the end of the descriptive entries.
The first entry stays whole.
Nothing is cut off in the middle of a claim.
never: Truncate in the middle of a sentence or claim.
why: A claim cut in half can say something false. Whole entries in, or whole entries out.
you_see: Remarks within the limit, made of whole entries.
test: Twenty long feature phrases. The draft is marked cut for length; entry 1 is there whole and entry 20 is gone.

title: Model drafting is on but the model has not passed its exam
when: You signed the drafting mode "model", but the active model has not passed the broker exam on the model actually being served.
steps: Agent 04 drafts by its rules instead of the model.
It tells you model drafting is on but was not used, and why.
never: Draft with a model that has not passed the exam.
why: A model writes fluently but can invent. Only an examined model on the served version may draft your listings.
you_see: A question saying model drafting was not used and why.
test: You sign drafting mode "model"; no examined model is being served. The listing is drafted by rules and goes to review as normal.

title: A model draft fails its checks
when: A model's draft has no recorded reasoning, is over the MLS limit, or contains a number that is not in the listing data.
steps: Agent 04 does not use the model's draft.
It drafts by rules and records why the model's draft was rejected.
never: Use a model draft that fails a check.
why: A number not in the data is invented. Reasoning that is missing cannot be checked. Either one disqualifies the draft.
you_see: The rules-based draft and the reason in the record.

title: Compliance flags a phrase inside model-written remarks
when: Compliance flags a phrase in remarks the model wrote.
steps: Agent 04 removes exactly the sentence that carries the phrase.
It resubmits the draft for review.
never: Rewrite the rest of the remarks, or leave the flagged sentence in.
why: Removing exactly the flagged sentence fixes the problem without changing anything Compliance already approved.
you_see: The remarks without the flagged sentence, after a new review.

title: Compliance flags a phrase Agent 04 cannot find in its draft
when: Compliance flags a phrase, but no single fact in the draft contains it (for example the phrase is split across two features).
steps: Agent 04 holds the draft for you.
It does not resubmit the same draft, and no copy is released.
never: Resubmit a draft unchanged after a flag.
why: Resubmitting the same text would loop forever or slip a flagged phrase through. A person has to look.
you_see: A question saying Compliance flagged a phrase Agent 04 could not find in its draft.
test: A new listing with features "perfect for" and "young families". Compliance reads the whole draft and flags the phrase; neither feature contains it alone.
